title: Ihsan: as if you see
hook: to worship Allah as though you see Him, for He sees you (Hadith of Jibril, Muslim)

segments.voice: Yesterday, tasawwuf, the inner path, and a hand on the heart. Your line was the heart is the house. What did you find in the room? Day two hundred ninety-four, the end of the week.

Medina. A small group of companions is sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a man walks up. His clothes are brilliantly white, his hair jet black. There's no dust on him, no sign he's traveled, and yet nobody there knows who he is. He walks right up, sits down facing the Prophet, knee to knee, and rests his hands on his thighs, like a student. And he starts asking questions. What is Islam? What is faith? And then the third question, the one Sufis would return to again and again: tell me about ihsan. Today, the answer.
screen: `A STRANGER IN WHITE.` → `KNEE TO KNEE, LIKE A STUDENT.` → `TELL ME ABOUT IHSAN.`

segments.voice: It's called the hadith of Jibril, and it comes at the start of Sahih Muslim's book of faith. The stranger asks about Islam, and the Prophet names the five pillars. He asks about iman, faith, and the Prophet names what Muslims believe in. Then he asks about ihsan, and the Prophet says: it is to worship God as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, then truly He sees you. When the stranger leaves, the Prophet tells them it was the angel Jibril, Gabriel, who came to teach them their religion. So the religion, in this hadith, has three floors. Islam, what you do. Iman, what you believe. Ihsan, how you do it, from the inside. The word comes from a root meaning beauty, goodness, doing something well. Ihsan is doing a thing beautifully. And notice the two steps in the answer. The first is a high one: worship as if you could see God. So there's a second step, a floor underneath: if you can't see Him, He sees you. You're not alone in the room. Sufis took ihsan as the name of their work, but the word belongs to every Muslim; the Qur'an says God loves the muhsinin, those who do ihsan. And it rounds off a week that began with a sickroom: let another lead, he smiled at the rows, the highest companion, God is alive, he left the way, the heart is the house. And now: as though you see Him.
screen: `THE HADITH OF JIBRIL.` · `ISLAM, IMAN, IHSAN.` · `AS THOUGH YOU SEE HIM.` · `IF NOT, HE SEES YOU.` · then, large: `AS THOUGH YOU SEE HIM.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do one prayer, or one act, as if seen. If you pray, choose your next prayer, and try it with that picture: as though you see God, and if you can't, knowing He sees you. Notice how your body changes, your pace, your attention. If you don't pray, take one ordinary act today, washing a cup, answering a message, and do it beautifully, as if the one you most respect were watching. For now, just sit and rehearse it. The bell holds the time.
Ihsan. Doing a thing beautifully: worshiping God as though you see Him, knowing that He sees you. Today's word.
Your line: as though you see him. Today, pick one small task and do it as if you were being watched with love. Day two hundred ninety-four.

howItsDone: Muslims learn the hadith of Jibril as a summary of the religion in three levels, islam, iman and ihsan, and prayer offered with that attention, as though seeing God, is what ihsan names.

original.note: Arabic: excellence, doing beautifully; from a root meaning beauty and goodness.

trapdoor: what it means: doing a thing beautifully, worshiping as though you see God, knowing He sees you.
what a scholar hears: the third level in the hadith of Jibril (Sahih Muslim 8), from the root h-s-n; the Qur'an's muhsinin are the people of ihsan.
